chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū  ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

A scholar came to a worshipper and said to him, 'How is your prayer?' He replied, 'You are asking me about my prayer while I have been worshipping Allah since such-and-such a time?' So he asked him, 'How is your weeping?' He replied, 'Verily I do not weep until my tears flow.' So the scholar said to him, 'Indeed your laughter while you fear Allah is better than your weeping while you are self-conceited before Allah! Verily the one who is self-conceited due to his actions has none of his deeds ascend [to Allah].'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between sincere worship and self-conceited worship in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the external form of worship and the internal state of the heart, critiquing the worshipper's *idāl* (self-admiration or pride in one's deeds). The scholar highlights that even joyous laughter rooted in God-consciousness (*khawf*) is superior to weeping driven by self-conceit, as pride acts as a veil that prevents deeds from ascending to the Divine. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and the subtle corruption of *riya* (showing off) even within long-standing acts of worship.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 3.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said, “

A scholar once came to a worshipper and said to him, ‘How is your prayer?’ He replied, ‘You are asking me about my prayer while I have been worshipping Allah since such-and-such a time?’ So he asked him, ‘How are you weeping?’ He replied, ‘Verily I weep until my tears flow [down my face].’ So the scholar said to him, ‘Indeed your laughter while you fear Allah is better than your weeping while you are self-conceited before Allah! Verily the one who is self-conceited due to his actions has none of his deeds ascend [to Allah].’”
